# Tracekit Box

> Tracekit Box runs an AI agent's job, or any untrusted command, in its own Firecracker micro-VM with no network card.
> Every way out goes through a door on the host: the network (an allowlist; private and cloud-metadata addresses are
> refused whatever the allowlist or an approval says), secrets (the VM holds only a placeholder; the real value is
> added on the way out, only for the hosts it is bound to), commands, and code changes (returned as a patch, each file
> decided before it is written back). A Tracekit signer the agent can't reach decides and signs each door, and each
> job exports one `.tkb` file anyone can verify offline. Open source (MIT), by Cygnux Labs. Status: v0, built from
> source, one Linux host with KVM.

Use it when an agent or a CI job must run code with real credentials, reach the network, or change a repository, and
someone needs to prove afterwards exactly what it did.

Needs: Linux (x86_64 or arm64) with `/dev/kvm`, or a GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner; `e2fsprogs` and `git`;
`tkbox` and its guest agent built from source (`make linux`, see the README's Install); a Tracekit 1.4.2 signer
(`pip install tracekit-ai==1.4.2`, then `tracekit init --dev --v2 --no-hooks && tracekit up --wait` for a same-user
dev signer, which gives dev assurance only).

## Run a job

```sh
tkbox daemon &                                   # once per host; `tkbox ls` answers once it is up
tkbox run --name job --image python:3.12-slim --allow pypi,debian --workspace . \
  --secret GH=env:GH_TOKEN@api.github.com        # the box sees only a placeholder for GH
tkbox exec job -- pip install -q pytest          # each command is decided by the signer first
tkbox exec job -- python -m pytest               # runs in /workspace, a copy of your checkout
tkbox approvals                                  # hosts off the allowlist wait here; `tkbox approve <id>` on the host
tkbox stop job && tkbox diff job                 # the job's changes, as a patch
tkbox apply job                                  # writes them to your checkout, each file decided first
tkbox export job -o job.tkb && tracekit verify job.tkb --trust job.trust.json   # Integrity: VERIFIED.
```

## From an agent (MCP)

`tkbox mcp` serves boxes as MCP tools over stdio: `tkbox_run`, `tkbox_exec`, `tkbox_diff`, `tkbox_stop`, `tkbox_ls`.
An MCP client can only narrow what the operator set up (image, allowlist, secrets, workspace roots, limits) and only
reach the boxes its own session created.

## In GitHub Actions

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    persist-credentials: false
- uses: Cygnux-Labs/tracekit-box/action@main
  with:
    agent: claude-code            # or codex, or command (with a `command:` input)
    prompt: "Make the failing test pass. Do not change the test."
  env:
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
```

The key reaches only the daemon on the runner; the box sees a placeholder that works only for `api.anthropic.com`.
The action applies the changes only if the signer allows every file and none is sensitive, and uploads the bundle,
its trust file and the patch as an artifact. Its signer is a dev signer made in the same job: dev assurance only.

## From Python

`pip install ./sdk/python` (from a checkout), then `from tracekit_box import Client`.
